\section{Convex cones}
\begin{definition}
A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a convex cone if $\alpha x + \beta y \in K$ for all $x,y\in K$ and $\alpha,\beta \ge 0$.
\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}
The dual cone $K^* = \{y \in \mathbb{R}^d : \langle x, y \rangle \ge 0 \text{ for all } x\in K\}$ is closed and convex.
\end{lemma}
\begin{theorem}[Bipolar identity]
If $K$ is a nonempty closed convex cone, then $(K^*)^* = K$.
\[
x \in K \iff \langle x, y \rangle \ge 0 \quad \forall y \in K^*.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Separation of a point $z \notin K$ from the closed convex cone $K$ yields a hyperplane passing through the origin.
\end{proof}
\begin{remark}
Closure is essential for the bipolar identity.
\end{remark}
